items.title: Every finite set of elements of a bounded above complex of free modules lies in a bounded subcomplex of finite free modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement takes a bounded above complex F of free R-modules and a finite list of elements f_i in various degrees, and asserts the existence of a bounded subcomplex G of F containing all of them whose terms are finite free (statement lines 38552-38559). The proof is a descending induction on the minimal degree that occurs, and the induction step has to handle two degrees at once: a finite set of basis elements of F^a is chosen to capture the given elements of that degree, and a second finite set of basis elements of F^{a+1} is chosen so that the differentials of the first set land inside the span of the second, which is exactly what makes the glued object a subcomplex rather than just a family of submodules (proof lines 38564-38576). The finite rank and the boundedness of the result come from the finiteness of the two chosen sets and from the induction hypothesis. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
